ruled_out_vectors.vector: H1: Tick crossing at exact boundary — liquidity not properly added/removed
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Swap step at exact tick boundary correctly applies amountIn + feeAmount >= amountOut. DynamicHelper.computeSwap correctly checks sqrtPriceCurrentX96 == nextTickSqrtPriceX96 before crossing. Test confirms conservation at boundary.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H2: Fixed height split rounds to zero on one side — free tokens
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: FixedHelper.swapByInput rejects zero-value swaps with FixedPool__ZeroValueSwap. When 1-wei input at 5% fee rounds to 0 after fee, the pool correctly reverts. Larger inputs produce proportional outputs bounded by reserves.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H3: 100% fee input accepted but output rejected — asymmetric extraction
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Input fee at 10000 BPS takes entire amount, leaving 0 for swap (0 output = no extraction). Output fee rejects 10000 BPS because denominator becomes 0 (div by zero). Asymmetry is intentional design, not exploitable.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H4: swapExtraData != 32 bytes — silent default leading to unexpected price movement
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Default sqrtPriceLimitX96 is MIN_SQRT_RATIO+1 (zeroForOne) or MAX_SQRT_RATIO-1 (oneForZero) — the widest valid range. This is the most conservative default (no unexpected price impact). Swap math with these limits is bounded.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H5: uint256 truncates on cast to uint128 in _getTokensOwed
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: The uint128 truncation is intentional Uniswap V3 design. For realistic (non-wrapping) fee growth deltas, mulDiv(delta, liquidity, Q128) fits uint128. The wrapping behavior is part of the fee growth accounting model.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H6: Division before multiplication truncation in TickMath
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: TickMath uses bit-manipulation lookup tables (not div-before-mul). Round-trip getSqrtPriceAtTick -> getTickAtSqrtPrice recovers tick exactly or tick-1 (floor rounding). 10000-run fuzz test confirms consistency.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H7: Assembly calldataload without masking — dirty high bits
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: No raw calldataload in user-facing functions. All assembly in math libraries operates on local variables and constants, not calldata. Solidity 0.8 strict ABI decoding validates and masks all calldata types.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H8: Append extra bytes to ABI-encoded call to control unexpected values
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Solidity 0.8.24 uses strict ABI decoding by default. Extra bytes in calldata cause the decoder to revert. The AMM uses standard typed parameters throughout.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H9: Call contract that returns fewer bytes — corrupted returndata
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: Pool type interfaces use typed Solidity returns that ABI decoder validates. Short returndata causes Solidity to revert. ERC-20 transfers use SafeTransferLib which handles both bool-returning and no-return tokens.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H10: Corrupt free memory pointer via assembly
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: All assembly blocks in TickMath, BitMath, SqrtPriceMath, and LiquidityMath are annotated 'memory-safe'. No assembly block modifies the free memory pointer (0x40). Pure computation only.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: H11: Force low-liquidity dust loop — harvest 1-wei truncation per iteration
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: At liquidity=1 with zero fee, 1-wei swap produces amountOut <= amountIn. At 5%+ fee, 1-wei input rounds to 0 output. 1000-iteration dust loop on dynamic pool produces 0 total output. Fixed pool correctly rejects zero-value swaps.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C18: CLOBHelper.calculateFixedInput uses mulDivRoundingUp — maker overpay
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: CLOB rounds output UP (taker-favorable), while SingleProvider rounds DOWN (protocol-favorable). At extreme prices the absolute difference grows with price_ratio^2, but relative error stays negligible. Maker sets their own price; not exploitable in a loop.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C26: Cetus precision extraction — computeRatioX96 overflow to near-zero price
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: computeRatioX96 returns 0 on overflow, but pool initialization and swap entry enforce MIN_SQRT_RATIO <= sqrtPriceX96 <= MAX_SQRT_RATIO. A zero price would be caught by the bound check. Near-min price swaps produce bounded output.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C27: Balancer rounding direction — dust loop drain via wrong rounding
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: All rounding in SqrtPriceMath, SwapMath, FixedHelper consistently rounds against the user. getAmount0Delta/getAmount1Delta(roundUp=true) >= getAmount0Delta/getAmount1Delta(roundUp=false). 1000-iteration dust loop confirms protocol balance never decreases.

DynamicPoolType uses direct liquidity amounts (not shares). LP specifies liquidityChange directly, so there is no share calculation that can be manipulated by donation. Both minimal (liq=1) and large (liq=1e18) deposits produce proportional, non-zero amounts.

ruled_out_vectors.vector: C29: Hook price manipulation — extreme price from hook return
ruled_out_vectors.why_ruled_out: computeSwap enforces sqrtPriceLimitX96 > MIN_SQRT_RATIO and < MAX_SQRT_RATIO. Near-zero and near-max target prices produce bounded swap outputs. A hook cannot set prices outside these bounds because the pool type validates price limits before calling computeSwap.
